# Compare two Excel files side-by-side using ChatGPT

**Hook:**
You’ve just received two Excel files from your team—one from last month, one from this month—and you need to spot what changed. Instead of scrolling through rows for ages, you can upload both files into ChatGPT and ask it to compare them. In a minute or two you’ll get a clear list of differences you can trust. This guide shows you how to do it step-by-step.

## Before you start
- A **computer** (Windows, Mac or Chromebook) with at least 4 GB of RAM.
- Two **Excel files** (.xlsx) you want to compare. They should have matching columns (for example, both have “Product”, “Sales”, “Region”).
- A **free ChatGPT account** (sign-up at [chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com)).
- Roughly **10 minutes** total time.

---

## Step 1 — Open ChatGPT in your browser
Open the web browser you usually use (like Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari) and type **chatgpt.com** in the address bar. Press Enter. You’ll see a page with a big green “Sign up” button on the right side and a smaller “Log in” link below it. Click whichever one you need. A sign-in box appears with options like “Continue with Google” or “Continue with Microsoft”. Choose the one you already use for email. After you sign in, the ChatGPT chat screen opens. You’ll see a message box in the centre and a few example prompts below it. You’ll know it worked when you see your name or email in the top-right corner and the message box is ready for typing.

💬 Example:
(No typing needed — just click the sign-in button.)

---

## Step 2 — Start a fresh chat
Look for a small **New chat** button in the top-left corner of the screen. It’s usually a plus sign or a little chat bubble. Click it. The screen refreshes and the message box clears. You’ll see the words “New Chat” at the top of the page and the chat history on the left side shows a single new chat with today’s date and time. You’ll know it worked when the chat list on the left shows a fresh chat with the current date and time.

💬 Example:
(You type nothing — just click the New chat button.)

---

## Step 3 — Upload your first Excel file
In the message box at the bottom, type **Upload a file** and press Enter. A file picker window opens. Navigate to your first Excel file on your computer, select it, and click Open. The file uploads and ChatGPT confirms it’s ready. You’ll see a small file icon and the file name appear in the chat. You’ll know it worked when the file name appears in the chat and you see a green checkmark next to it.

💬 Example:
(You type nothing — just pick the file from your computer.)

---
## Step 4 — Upload your second Excel file
Repeat Step 3 to upload your second Excel file. ChatGPT now has both files in the chat. You’ll see both file names listed, one after the other. If the upload takes longer than a few seconds, you’ll see a spinning circle. You’ll know it worked when both file names appear in the chat with green checkmarks.

💬 Example:
(You type nothing — just pick the second file from your computer.)

---
## Step 5 — Ask ChatGPT to compare the files
In the message box at the bottom, type:
**Compare these two Excel files and list the differences in a table.**

Then press Enter. ChatGPT starts processing. It reads both files, compares the data row by row, and prepares a summary. You’ll see a spinning icon or a “Processing…” message while it works. After a few seconds, a table appears showing rows that differ, with columns like “Row”, “Column”, “Value in File 1”, and “Value in File 2”. You’ll know it worked when you see a clear table of differences in the chat.

💬 Example:
Compare these two Excel files and list the differences in a table.

---
## Step 6 — Review the differences table
Scan the table ChatGPT produced. Each row shows a cell that changed between the two files. Look for the “Value in File 1” and “Value in File 2” columns to see what actually changed. If the table is too long, ask ChatGPT to:
**Show only rows where Sales changed by more than 10%.**

ChatGPT will filter the table. You’ll know it worked when the table is shorter and focuses on the biggest differences.

💬 Example:
Show only rows where Sales changed by more than 10%.

---
## Step 7 — Ask for a summary or export
If you want a quick summary, type:
**Summarise the key differences in three bullet points.**

ChatGPT writes a short summary you can copy into an email or note. If you want to save the table, ask:
**Export the differences table as a CSV file.**

ChatGPT creates a download link. Click it to save the file to your computer. You’ll know it worked when you see a download link or a summary that makes sense.

💬 Example:
Summarise the key differences in three bullet points.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Uploading files with different column names**: ChatGPT compares column by column. If the columns don’t match (for example, one file has “Revenue” and the other has “Income”), the comparison will miss data or give errors. Fix: Rename columns in both files so they match exactly before uploading.
- **Ignoring the processing time**: If your files are large (over 10,000 rows), ChatGPT may take longer than a few seconds. Fix: Wait patiently; don’t close the browser or refresh the page until you see the results.
- **Assuming every difference is important**: ChatGPT lists every change, even tiny ones like a space in a product name. Fix: Use the “Show only rows where…” prompt to filter for meaningful differences.

---
## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You manage budgets or track inventory across months. Instead of opening two Excel files and squinting at rows, you upload them to ChatGPT and get a clean list of changes in seconds. You save time and avoid mistakes.
- **For your business or work:** Your team shares monthly sales reports in Excel. When a manager asks “What changed from last month?”, you can run this comparison in minutes and send a clear summary. No more guessing or manual scanning.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with two small Excel files (under 5,000 rows). Once you see how easy it is, you’ll trust ChatGPT for bigger files and more complex comparisons.

---
## Try it now
Open [chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com), sign in, and upload two small Excel files you already have. Ask ChatGPT to compare them and list the differences. You’ll have your answer in under two minutes.
